question: Can a polysemantic image-model neuron be decomposed into several human-coherent concept directions using only its maximally activating examples?

key_findings.claim: The proposed pipeline treats polysemanticity as multimodality among a neuron's top-activating input representations rather than as an indivisible property of its scalar activation.
key_findings.evidence: For a selected neuron, the method retrieves its highest-activation images, computes distances in the surrounding layer activation space, clusters those examples, and uses each cluster to define a distinct linear concept vector.

key_findings.claim: Concept-vector projections can re-rank inputs so that visually distinct modes of one neuron's preferred set become separately controllable.
key_findings.evidence: Case studies for chosen vision-model neurons show different clusters corresponding to recognizable motifs; projecting on the associated vector raises examples from its cluster while lowering competing modes, with adjustable separation strength.

key_findings.claim: A small human odd-one-out test provides some evidence that the separated sets are perceptually coherent, but it is not a causal validation of model behavior.
key_findings.evidence: Eight participants judge visual grouping consistency for the concept-conditioned examples. The evaluation measures human coherence of selected images, not whether intervention along the vector changes the network's class decision through the claimed mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The method is discovery-assisted rather than fully automatic interpretability because neuron choice, cluster count, linkage, labels, and displayed examples all admit analyst discretion.
key_findings.evidence: The paper demonstrates a limited set of selected neurons with agglomerative clustering and qualitative labels. Appendix dendrograms expose alternate grouping levels, and no large-scale stability or selection-corrected metric is reported.

method.core_idea: Split a neuron's top-activating examples into activation-space clusters and convert each cluster into a linear direction that isolates one semantic mode.
method.mechanism: The algorithm gathers maximally activating images for a target unit, clusters their full layer representations using Euclidean distance and Ward linkage, fits/derives a concept vector per cluster, and projects activations to rank images by each disentangled direction. Qualitative visualization and an odd-one-out study assess coherence.
assumptions: A polysemantic neuron's concepts form separable clusters among its most activating samples.
Euclidean layer distance and hierarchical clustering preserve the semantic distinctions of interest.
A linear concept direction adequately represents each cluster beyond the selected samples.
Human visual coherence is a meaningful proxy for mechanistic interpretability.

techniques.role: Constructs a neuron-specific dataset enriched for its encoded modes.
Separates top activations into candidate semantic concepts.
Represents each discovered mode as a direction in activation space.
Tests whether concept-conditioned image sets are perceptually coherent.

evaluations.setting: Selected polysemantic neurons in an image classification network.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative separation of maximally activating image modes and projected rankings.
evaluations.result: Several neurons decompose into visually coherent concept groups whose rankings can be adjusted independently.
evaluations.baseline: The original scalar neuron ranking without cluster-specific directions.

evaluations.setting: Concept-vector strength sweeps on the demonstrated neurons.
evaluations.metric: Visual purity/separation of examples associated with each vector.
evaluations.result: Increasing the vector contribution sharpens the reported concept separation, though no causal class-output metric is supplied.

evaluations.setting: Odd-one-out judgments by eight human participants.
evaluations.result: Participants generally recognize the separated groups, supporting face validity at small scale.
evaluations.baseline: Image groups formed from the undiscriminated polysemantic neuron.

limitations: Only a small selected set of vision neurons and concepts is shown.
The human study has eight participants and limited statistical power.
No causal activation patching or downstream-output intervention tests vector necessity or sufficiency.
Clustering choices and semantic names are analyst-dependent and no cross-seed/corpus stability is measured.
failure_modes: Top-activation sampling can omit concepts encoded at moderate activation levels.
Hierarchical clustering may split one concept by background or merge distinct concepts sharing texture.
A direction fitted to selected images may not generalize beyond that sample set.
Human-friendly clusters can be epiphenomenal to the model's actual decision pathway.
reusable_insights: Condition the interpretability dataset on a unit before searching for its internal modes.
Evaluate a concept direction on held-out preimages and causal interventions, not only representative visualizations.
Dendrogram level and cluster stability should be exposed to the user instead of hiding one chosen decomposition.
open_questions: Can the method scale automatically to every neuron and report false-discovery-controlled concepts?
Do cluster-derived vectors causally control model predictions or only retrieve coherent images?
How does the approach compare with overcomplete sparse features when concepts overlap rather than cluster cleanly?

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV)
competitive_landscape.relationship: Represents user-defined concepts as activation-space directions and measures class sensitivity along them.
competitive_landscape.difference: TCAV starts from labeled concept examples and supplies a directional-derivative test; this paper discovers several candidate concepts by clustering one neuron's top activations.

competitive_landscape.title: Network Dissection: Quantifying Interpretability of Deep Visual Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Labels individual CNN units by alignment with a broad externally annotated visual-concept set.
competitive_landscape.difference: Network Dissection quantifies monosemantic alignment at scale; this work specifically decomposes a selected polysemantic unit into multiple directions without a concept segmentation dictionary.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
competitive_landscape.relationship: Studies how learned sparse features and higher-order concept structure occupy activation space.
competitive_landscape.difference: Sparse autoencoders learn an overcomplete dictionary across all activations; the concept-vector paper operates post hoc on top samples of one neuron and uses clustering to split its modes.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Polysemantic neurons can be disentangled into distinct concept vectors by clustering their maximally activating representations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Selected unit case studies and a small human judgment experiment show visually coherent, separately ranked modes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The neuron-conditioned clustering recipe is intuitive and useful for exploration, but evidence is too small and noncausal to establish general mechanistic disentanglement.

reviewer_notes: Read all eight cached pages, including dendrograms and additional visualizations. Concept-direction, unit-labeling, and sparse-feature competitors were checked at primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
